Part 82 requires that an Ext. D&C lake made on a clay substratum using calcium as the basic radical is permitted, provided it meets the specifications for lakes defined under §82.2051. The lake must be prepared by extending one of the straight colors (e.g., Ext. D&C Yellow No. 2) with calcium and applied to a substratum such as clay; however, the specific color or type of lake is not restricted by the substrate alone—only that the preparation follows the general rules for lakes in §82.2051.

21 CFR 82.2051(a)(1) [1] permits lakes made from a straight color (e.g., Ext. D&C Yellow No. 2) extended on substrata such as clay, titanium dioxide, or zinc oxide, provided the lake is formed by combining the basic radical calcium with one of the listed straight colors.

21 CFR 82.2051(a)(2) [2] and [3] require that ether extracts shall not exceed 0.5 percent; soluble chlorides and sulfates (as sodium salts) shall not exceed 3.0 percent; and intermediates shall not exceed 0.2 percent.

21 CFR 82.2051(b) [4] states each lake made as prescribed in paragraph (a) is considered a straight color and listed under the name formed by combining the original color name, the basic radical used, and the word “Lake.”

21 CFR 82.2051(b)(1) [5] requires that the listed name of the color from which the lake is prepared be included in the name.

21 CFR 82.2051(b)(2) [6] requires that the name of the basic radical combined in such color (e.g., calcium) be included in the name.

21 CFR 82.2051(b)(3) [7] requires that the word “Lake” be appended to the name, as in "Ext. D&C Yellow No. 2—Calcium Lake."

21 CFR 82.2050 [8] requires a batch of a straight color (including lakes) to conform to §82.5 and to the specifications set forth in this subpart for such color to be certified for use in externally applied drugs and cosmetics.
